title: Emergency planning zone reform for small reactors
bottleneck: Current emergency planning rules were written for gigawatt plants and can require evacuation planning over 10-mile zones, absurd for a microreactor with a fraction of the source term, yet legally required until regulators grant exemptions. The NRC has proposed scalable, dose-based EPZ rules, but implementation is slow and contested. EPZ requirements can single-handedly kill otherwise viable siting. Until rules change, developers must either seek case-by-case exemptions, a slow and uncertain process, or overbuild emergency planning they do not need.
why_it_blocks: Regulatory overhead scaled for large plants makes small reactors uneconomic. If a 10 MW microreactor needs the same emergency planning as a 1 GW plant, its cost advantage vanishes.
current_state: The NRC issued guidance allowing smaller EPZs with justification. Risk-informed, dose-based EPZ rulemaking is progressing but incomplete.
